Stage 2 — the reference bundle

Source: R/pipeline.R
pf_reference.Rd

Returns the reference the cascade matches against, with the stage-4 recovery keys (pf_add_recovery_keys()) added, so the bundle is complete. This is preprocessing and is excluded from match timings.

Usage

pf_reference(
  bmf = NULL,
  cache = "data-dev/BMF-REFERENCE-BUNDLE.rds",
  active_col = NULL,
  recovery = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  source = c("auto", "matchdb", "local"),
  tier = getOption("pfmatch.matchdb_tier", "active-observed")
)

Arguments

bmf

Processed BMF: a path or a data frame. Needed only for the local bundle, and only when cache does not exist.

cache

Path to cache the local bundle (.rds). NULL disables caching.

active_col

Optional BMF-active flag column (local bundle only).

recovery

Add acronym / prefix blocking keys to the reference.

verbose

Print progress.

source

"auto", "matchdb" or "local"; see above.

tier

The matchdb tier. Defaults to getOption("pfmatch.matchdb_tier", "active-observed").

Value

A reference bundle: reference, name_freq, token_idf, ref_index, and source ("matchdb" or "local"). A matchdb bundle also carries clusters and its publication stamp.

Where the reference comes from

source = "matchdb"

A published matchdb reference, matchdb::md_reference(tier, fetch = "missing"): downloaded once from the public NCCS copy, checked against its md5s and against the installed npmatch normalizer, and cached under matchdb's data root. Nothing is built locally.

source = "local"

The bundle built here from bmf by pf_build_reference(), cached at cache.

source = "auto" (the default)

A bmf given is a request for that file, so it is honoured: the local bundle, exactly as before. Without one, matchdb when the package is installed and the tier loads; otherwise, with a message saying why, the local bundle at cache. A matchdb bundle built by a different npmatch normalizer is refused by md_reference(), so a normalizer update falls back here until the tier is republished.

tier = "active-observed" is the default because it wins on both axes at once: the bmf_active layer with legal, DBA and observed name variants, 2.89M rows, it matched the 1k benchmark in 11.5 min against 23.2 for the augmented BMF pfmatch built for itself, and cleared 63.8% against 62.8% (dev/BENCH-MD-REFERENCE.log). "unified-observed" is the closer correspondence to the augmented bundle — it adds the inactive tranche, so every BMF release rather than the current one — but that is 1.76M more rows for two and a half times the match time and +0.1 point. Ask for it when the question is grantees that no longer exist, not for the clear rate. The "Choosing a matching dictionary" vignette has the comparison; matchdb::md_reference() lists the tiers.
